clue.text: Bird, black one, is carrying …

indicators.note: the word is holds the other letters inside it, as a bearer carries a load

parts.note: taken as written
B is the standard abbreviation for black, as on pencils
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher's note trails off: a dark bird, one in particular, is carrying something.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs this clue on into the next one; it has no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The ibis is a long-legged wading bird with a downcurved bill.

clue.text: … plant having purple shoot and orange tip

parts.note: plum is a dark reddish-purple colour
to bag game is to shoot it

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its first letter here, the top of orange

explanation.surface: Continuing from the bird, a plant with purple shoots and orange-tipped flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: Plumbago, also called leadwort, is a flowering shrub often grown for its pale blue blooms.

clue.text: Grey leader dropped behind

indicators.note: the first letter of the synonym is let fall

parts.note: drear means dull and grey, as of weather

explanation.surface: A horse called Grey, once the leader, has dropped back in the race.
explanation.definitionFit: The rear is the back part, so as a noun it means the behind or bottom.

clue.text: Bonxie's true blue

parts.note: the setter Bonxie speaking of himself: Bonxie is, so I am, I'M
proper means genuine or true, as in a proper job

explanation.surface: The setter declares himself a true-blue loyalist.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often write their own pseudonym for I or ME; here Bonxie's stands for I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue jokes are risqué ones, and improper means indecent in the same way.

clue.text: Express dismay at obscenities

definitions.meaning: to swear at something in annoyance

explanation.definitionFit: To curse is to swear angrily, and curses are swear words themselves.

clue.text: Pole takes back nothing on board — food's thin

indicators.note: the pole receives the other letters into its middle

parts.note: a mast is a tall upright pole

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece written on another sits beneath it, so nothing comes after the board
the word for board is read from right to left

parts.note: a table is a board, as in board and lodging
the letter O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A Polish visitor takes nothing back on board ship, so his food is meagre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the board word to give ELBAT; the Pole here is a post, not a Polish person.
explanation.definitionFit: Melba toast is very thin crisp toast, so this is a thin food.

clue.text: Yellow bird caught first

indicators.note: tells us the cricket letter goes at the front

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
the raven is a large black bird

explanation.surface: A yellow bird was caught before any other.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellow is slang for cowardly, and craven means cowardly too.

clue.text: Mineral regularly seen on pearls

indicators.note: take every other letter of the words on pearls, starting with the first

explanation.surface: A gemstone often seen set beside pearls in jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: Opal is a mineral, a form of silica prized as a gemstone.

clue.text: Blue spray applied over green swelling

indicators.note: the scattered letters are laid over and around the next one
spraying scatters the letters of blue into a new order

parts.note: G is a standard abbreviation for green

explanation.surface: Blue paint sprayed over a green surface leaves a lump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spray' rearranges BLUE into BULE, which closes around G.
explanation.definitionFit: A bulge is a rounded protrusion, a swelling outwards.

clue.text: Long-running show from Jerry Springer?

definitions.meaning: Agatha Christie's play The ..., running in London since 1952
Jerry is the mouse in Tom and Jerry, and a springer is something that springs: a device that springs on a mouse

explanation.surface: Is the Jerry Springer talk show a long-running hit?
explanation.definitionFit: The Mousetrap is the world's longest-running stage play; a mouse trap is a spring device for catching mice.

clue.text: Cut flower attached to back of black hats

indicators.note: the cut flower follows the word for black

parts.note: sombre means dark or black, as of colours

indicators.note: cutting removes the final letter

parts.note: the rose is a flower

explanation.surface: Cut flowers pinned to the back of black hats.
explanation.definitionFit: Sombreros are wide-brimmed Mexican hats.

clue.text: It flies round violet at first, having left slope

indicators.note: the insect goes around the next letter

parts.note: a bee is something that flies

indicators.note: only the opening letter of violet is wanted

explanation.surface: An insect circles a violet and then leaves, going down a slope.
explanation.definitionFit: A bevel is a sloping edge cut on wood or glass.

clue.text: Pink mollusc

definitions.meaning: to pink is to cut a zigzag or wavy edge in cloth
a bivalve shellfish with a fan-shaped shell

explanation.definitionFit: To scallop is to cut an edge into curves, like pinking; the scallop is also an edible shellfish.

clue.text: Black horses unseating head trainers

indicators.note: throwing off a rider, so one letter is removed

parts.note: a stable is a group of racehorses kept together

indicators.note: the head of trainers is its first letter

explanation.surface: Black horses throw the leading trainers off.
explanation.definitionFit: Sable is the heraldic term for black.

clue.text: Tears after yellow sweets

indicators.note: the tears come after the colour

parts.note: lemon is a pale yellow colour
teardrops, so drops

explanation.surface: Someone cries after eating yellow sweets.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemon drops are boiled sweets flavoured with lemon.

clue.text: Black bag with belt I tucked inside

indicators.note: the next letters are placed within the bag

parts.note: a sac is a bag-like pouch
to tan is to beat or belt someone
taken as written

explanation.surface: A black bag with a belt that I have tucked inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Black magic is satanic, devilish and evil.

clue.text: Pink rock with trademark centre

indicators.note: the trademark symbol sits at the centre of the rock

parts.note: coal is a sedimentary rock
R in a circle is the registered trademark symbol

explanation.surface: A pink stick of seaside rock with a trademark through the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: Seaside rock is a British hard candy stick with lettering running through it.
explanation.definitionFit: Coral is a pinkish-orange colour, named after the sea creature.

clue.text: Large mushroom found outside, possibly pink

indicators.note: the boom word surrounds the size letter

parts.note: to mushroom is to grow rapidly, to boom

explanation.surface: A large mushroom found outdoors, maybe pink in colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A pink is a garden flower, so a bloom is possibly one.

clue.text: Red and green

definitions.meaning: ... as in red and sore, like ... skin

explanation.definitionFit: Raw skin is red and inflamed; a raw recruit is green and untrained.

clue.text: White man embraces first lover with abandon

parts.note: wan means pale or white

indicators.note: the man's name holds the next letter inside

parts.note: Tony is a man's name

indicators.note: only the first letter of lover

explanation.surface: A pale man hugs his first lover passionately.
explanation.definitionFit: Wantonly means recklessly or without restraint, which is acting with abandon.

clue.text: Yellow gong clasped by a monarch

indicators.note: the honour is held between the outer letters

parts.note: taken as written
R for rex or regina, king or queen
British slang for a medal or honour, such as the MBE (Member of the Order of the British Empire)

explanation.surface: A yellow medal pinned on by a king.
explanation.definitionFit: Amber is a yellowish-orange colour, as in the traffic light.

clue.text: Return to heartless African region for orange

indicators.note: everything that follows is read backwards
the middle letter is removed

parts.note: the Maghreb is north-west Africa

explanation.surface: Going back to a ruined part of Africa for an orange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes H from MAGHREB, giving MAGREB; 'Return' turns TO MAGREB into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The bergamot is a bitter citrus fruit, a kind of orange used to flavour Earl Grey tea.

clue.text: With a little space, he can generate lift

parts.note: an en is a small printer's space, half an em

indicators.note: to generate is to produce something new, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Given a bit of room, he can produce lift for the aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: To enhance is to raise or improve something, to give it a lift.

clue.text: Primary element — brown earth by estuary

parts.note: hydrogen, element number one, symbol H
umber is a natural brown earth pigment

explanation.surface: A geography note about a basic element and brown soil by an estuary.
explanation.definitionFit: The Humber is a large tidal estuary on England's east coast.

clue.text: Squire loosened corset

indicators.note: loosening the laces lets the letters of corset fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A gallant gentleman loosens a lady's corset.
explanation.definitionFit: To squire a lady is to escort or accompany her.

clue.text: Round brown flower organically produced

indicators.note: the colour word is turned round

parts.note: tan is a light brown
something that flows, a river: the Ural in Russia

explanation.surface: A round brown flower grown organically.
explanation.definitionFit: Natural products come from nature, not synthesised, as organic ones do.

clue.text: Pretend singer knocks top off dimmer switch

indicators.note: switching the letters around puts them in a new order
the first letter of dimmer is removed

explanation.surface: A fake singer knocks the knob off a dimmer switch.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing D leaves IMMER, which 'switch' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A mimer mimes, pretending to sing to a recorded track.

clue.text: Blue sponge with shape like a catapult

parts.note: to mop is to sponge up
the letter Y is shaped like a forked catapult

explanation.surface: A blue sponge shaped like a catapult.
explanation.definitionFit: Mopy means low in spirits, as feeling blue does.

clue.text: Brown drink the company distributed externally

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit outside the drink
the letters are spread out and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
cola is a fizzy drink

explanation.surface: A brown drink handed out by the company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distributed' rearranges the letters to give CHOTE; 'the' looks like a plain article but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Chocolate is a dark brown colour.

clue.text: Brown lid removed from kiln

indicators.note: the top letter of the word comes off

parts.note: to toast bread is to brown it

explanation.surface: Brown lid taken off a kiln.
explanation.definitionFit: An oast is a kiln for drying hops.

clue.text: The colour of a battlecruiser

indicators.note: the colour comes out of the word, its letters sitting inside it

explanation.surface: What colour is a battleship painted?
explanation.definitionFit: Ecru is a pale greyish-yellow colour of unbleached linen.

clue.text: Are purple letters moved just after delivery?

indicators.note: the letters are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: Are the purple letters moved just after they are delivered?
explanation.definitionFit: Puerperal describes the period just after childbirth, and delivery is giving birth.

clue.text: Retracts apologetic outburst right on track

indicators.note: draws back, so the exclamation reads backwards

parts.note: oops, said after a blunder

explanation.surface: Someone takes back an apology on the right track.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoor is the track or trail of an animal.
